mechanism_narrative: INSR (RTK, Tyr kinase) and IL6ST (gp130, JAK-associated cytokine receptor) are forced into proximity by a rigid 60 Å α-helical linker. INSR's intrinsic tyrosine kinase transphosphorylates IL6ST's ICD tyrosines, creating novel docking sites for GRB2, SHC1, PIK3R1, and STAT3, while JAK1/JAK2 from IL6ST reciprocally phosphorylate INSR tyrosines to recruit IRS1/IRS2 and PTPN11. The biased output is MAPK/ERK + PI3K/AKT + JAK/STAT3 signaling, with PLCγ1 and CBL sterically excluded by the rigid geometry. This shifts aged muscle toward a young transcriptional phenotype by upregulating contractile structural genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11) and downregulating aged inflammatory IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32).
